newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen marking time ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen marking time ahead of budget.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks are expected to mark time on Wednesday as investors await the 1997 state budget to be presented at 2:30 pm (0830 GMT), brokers said.
"Most orders are on hold as retail and institutional investors have adopted a wait-and-see attitude," said Chaminda Perera, a broker at Jardine Fleming HNB. "No one wants to take any chances."

Stocks closed firmer on Tuesday with the all share index up by 2.1 points at 617.3, driven mainly by small retailers' optimism on Wednesday's budget and a pre-arranged sale of a large blue-chip parcel.
Retail investors, anticipating a market-friendly 1997 budget have been pushing the market up in recent weeks.
Prasanna Chandrasekera, a trader at brokerage John Keells, said the market, which closes before the budget release, could move in a narrow range.
"The budget optimism can continue today," he said. "At the same time some people might want to move out and take profit."

Brokers said U.S. President Bill Clinton's victory was unlikely to have a major impact on the market except in the long-term if big funds bullish on U.S. stocks and money markets pulled cash out of Asia.
